key_insight: The study uses diffusion-based inpainting to generate realistic healthy mammograms by removing lesion regions, then uses these counterfactual images to improve classifier training.
clinical_relevance: This approach aims to reduce false negatives in breast cancer screening by making CAD systems more sensitive while preserving high specificity.
method: Train a DDPM on healthy BI-RADS 1 mammograms.
Use RePaint-style inpainting to replace annotated lesion boxes with realistic normal tissue.
Augment training data and test across ConvNeXt, ViT, Mammo-CLIP, and FPN-MIL models.
evidence_signal: On the VinDr-Mammo dataset, the counterfactual augmentation improved sensitivity across all evaluated architectures, especially at 80% fixed specificity, and radiologists judged the generated images to be realistic.
watch_item: Performance gains were shown on one dataset and depend on accurate lesion annotations and faithful image synthesis, so generalization and clinical robustness still need validation.
paper_title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation via Diffusion Inpainting for Mammography Classification
